unit.why: A short legend, quoted from the Hida's Shem ha-Gedolim, about R. Meir Gavizon, a pre-Hasidic judge accused of bribery whose sight was restored after he prayed; it sits inside a halakhic discussion of judges and bribery.
unit.boundary_note: The closing words 'מענין שוחט.' are a section heading that belongs to the next division.

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ שה״ג להג׳ חיד״א (מער' מ אות ט)
stories.end_quote: על קברו נענש. תנצב"ה זכותו יגן עלינו
stories.summary_en: R. Meir Gavizon, a blind judge rumored to have taken bribes, publicly prayed that God restore his sight if he was innocent; his prayer was answered, as the Hida confirmed by comparing his signatures from before and after, and anyone who swears falsely at his grave is punished.

tags.why: Praise of a pre-Hasidic Sephardi sage, copied from the Hida
